problems.source_says: Elaboration was scored by two blinded, trained raters, but their occupations and domain expertise are not stated anywhere in the document. The codebook defines human_raters as lay raters or crowd workers and expert_raters as domain experts, instructors, or professionals. Human scoring is established, but the specific lay/crowd classification is not; the measure category should be null pending clarification, retaining the reported rater description in measure_detail. This does not undermine scored_on_output or criterion 3.
problems.quote:
Two blinded, trained raters scored all 
submissions across Fluency (count of distinct, task-appropriate concepts), Flexibility (number 
of distinct conceptual domains utilized), and Elaboration (rated on a 1–5 rubric evaluating 
structural depth).
problems.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4 item 1; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, Measure table, lines 93-94. All 12 PDF pages checked for further rater qualifications.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1, S1-O2 and S1-O3 are expert ratings of produced project briefs, not self-reports: six domain experts rated originality, overall creativity and appropriateness on 1-7 scales; alpha = .91. The novelty, overall_creativity and usefulness constructs match these measures.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4 item 2; definitions of originality and appropriateness on PDF p. 2 (printed p. 180), Section 2.1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 and S1-O5 count task-appropriate concepts and conceptual domains in student submissions. They support fluency and within-person flexibility, both measured by category_count.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4 item 1; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 181), Section 2.1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 is an output-based elaboration score using a 1-5 structural-depth rubric; kappa = .88 is reported for the TTCT coding. Only the raters' lay-versus-expert classification is unconfirmed.

The AI arms had an LLM interface during task production. Initial unaided ideation in the scaffolded arm precedes AI use, and the no-copying rule does not state that AI was removed. Thus S1-O1 through S1-O6 answer with_ai and S1-O7 through S1-O8 answer across_people; no after_ai outcome is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Section 3.1, conditions 2-3 and CARP phases A-C; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Sections 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 186), Section 5.2.

confirmed.statement: The paper describes two tasks in one 90-minute session and explicitly characterizes the study as evaluating immediate creative output. No delayed output assessment or research appendix is present.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.3; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 189), Section 8 item 1; complete markdown lines 1-479 and PDF pp. 1-12, ending in references.

confirmed.statement: The participant unit for S1-O1 through S1-O6 is supported by composite ratings with 160 participants per arm, N = 480 and univariate degrees of freedom (2, 477); Table 1 does not analyze the individual expert ratings as separate observations.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Section 3.1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1 headers, note and test degrees of freedom.

confirmed.statement: Every Table 1 mean, SD, arm count, F statistic, degrees of freedom, p threshold and eta-squared in all 18 contrasts for S1-O1 through S1-O6 matches the PDF table exactly. Omnibus statistics are correctly identified as three-arm tests.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1, independently recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 correctly preserves originality d = -1.34, 0.61 and 2.23 with pairwise p < .001, and flags the abstract's conflicting d = -0.58 rather than replacing it.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Section 4.1 post-hoc paragraphs; PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 187), Discussion box.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 correctly preserves the conflicting fluency results: Table 1 F = 284.15 and eta-squared = .543 versus abstract F = 48.21 and eta-squared = .168, all with df (2, 477) and p < .001. The unconstrained-versus-control pairwise p < .001 is explicit.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1 and Section 4.1; PDF p. 1 (printed p. 179), Abstract.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 correctly records scaffolded flexibility exceeding both other groups at p < .001. The paper supplies no additional pairwise tests for overall creativity, appropriateness, elaboration, or the other fluency/flexibility contrasts; their directions follow the printed means.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 184), Table 1 and Section 4.1 post-hoc paragraphs; complete results and discussion, PDF pp. 6-10.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 correctly transcribes the Discussion box's Elaboration: +58% Increase as a separate printed claim whose calculation is not supplied.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 187), The Generative AI Creativity Paradox box.

confirmed.statement: S1-O7 compares different students' submissions within each condition and task using pairwise cosine similarity, supporting diversity, embedding_similarity and across_people. The paper names text-embedding-3-large and states 1536 dimensions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4 item 3; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Section 4.2.

confirmed.statement: All three S1-O7 contrasts reproduce Table 2 exactly: control 0.412 (0.084), dispersion 0.588; unconstrained 0.689 (0.061), dispersion 0.311; scaffolded 0.465 (0.072), dispersion 0.535. The unconstrained/control t(318) = 34.21, p < .001 and d = 3.79 also match; directions correctly refer to diversity rather than similarity.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Table 2 and Section 4.2; table independently recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables.

confirmed.statement: S1-O7 appropriately leaves unit and n_units null: pairwise construction is described, but the observations used for the t-test, the SD basis and aggregation across tasks are not specified. No scaffolded pairwise test is printed.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 183), Section 3.4 item 3; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Table 2 and Section 4.2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O8 accurately retains the descriptive 71% recurring-theme finding from cross-comparison of unconstrained essays. The output unit and across-person diversity interpretation are supported; the coding method, essay count, uncertainty and comparator are absent, as the form states.

No additional scored creativity or across-person diversity outcome was found. Table 3 models the already-recorded originality outcome, while the 88.4% finding measures adoption of an AI-provided option rather than an additional creativity rating or comparison between people's outputs.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8 (printed pp. 185-186), Section 4.3, Table 3 and Section 5.1; full markdown and PDF reviewed through the final references page.

summary: Output-scoring eligibility holds, and the recorded numerical results match the cited PDF passages. S1-O6's human_raters code is unsupported under the codebook's lay/crowd definition because the paper identifies only trained raters without specifying their qualifications.
